# add-greeting: let alpha produce a greeting that beta prints

- size: project
- owner: demo-owner
- repos: [alpha, beta]
- supersedes: []
- approved: demo-owner 2026-10-01T09:00Z

## Why

Users of `beta` want a greeting on start-up, and the text belongs in `alpha`,
the shared library, so that other tools can use it too.

## Scope

In: the greeting text in `alpha`; printing it in `beta`.

Out: translations; any change to `gamma`.

## Requirements

### R1 Greeting text
`alpha` SHALL provide the greeting `hello, demo` for a caller that asks for it.

#### R1.S1 Default greeting
- GIVEN `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with no name
- THEN it gets the exact text `hello, demo` (11 characters, no trailing
  newline)

#### R1.S2 Name too long
- GIVEN a name of 65 characters
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with that name
- THEN it gets an error naming the 64-character limit, and no greeting

### R2 beta prints the greeting
`beta` SHALL print the greeting from `alpha` as its first line of output.

#### R2.S1 Start-up line
- GIVEN `beta` built against `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN `beta` starts with no arguments
- THEN its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of
  start (wall time)

## Approaches

1. Greeting in `alpha`, printed by `beta` (picked: one source of the text).
2. Greeting in `beta` only (rejected: other tools would copy the text).

## Open calls

1. The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points.
# add-greeting plan

- change: add-greeting
- spec: changes/add-greeting/spec.md

## 1 Goal and approach

Put the greeting text in `alpha` behind one function, and have `beta` print
it on start-up. Two build tasks, one per repo, with `beta`'s after `alpha`'s.

## 2 Interface contract

- `alpha`: `greeting(name: str | None = None) -> str`, in `alpha/greeting.py`.
  With no name it returns `hello, demo`. A name of more than 64 code points
  raises `ValueError`, whose message names the 64-character limit.
- `beta`: `python3 -m beta`, run in the `beta` checkout with the `alpha`
  checkout beside it, prints `greeting()` as its first line.

## 3 Global constraints

- "The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points." (spec,
  Open calls 1)
- "its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of start
  (wall time)" (spec, R2.S1)
- Every number carries its unit.

## 4 File map

- alpha: `alpha/greeting.py` (the greeting and the name limit),
  `tests/test_greeting.py`.
- beta: `beta/__main__.py` (the start-up line), `tests/test_main.py`.

## 5 Tasks

### T1 Greeting text in alpha
- role: build
- repo: alpha
- after: []
- runs: mesh
- needs: any
- serves: [R1]
- touches: alpha/greeting.py, tests/test_greeting.py
- produces: greeting(name: str | None = None) -> str
- steps: failing test, watch it fail, minimal code, watch it pass, commit
- done when: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` passes in
  alpha at the branch head, and the T4 review has no Critical or
  Important finding

### T2 beta prints the greeting
- role: build
- repo: beta
- after: [T1]
- runs: mesh
- needs: any
- serves: [R2]
- touches: beta/__main__.py, tests/test_main.py
- consumes: greeting() from T1
- steps: failing test, watch it fail, minimal code, watch it pass, commit
- done when: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` passes in
  beta at the branch head, and the T5 review has no Critical or
  Important finding

## 6 Test tasks

### T3 Scenario tests R1.S1 to R2.S1
- role: test
- repo: space
- after: []
- runs: mesh
- needs: any
- serves: [R1, R2]
- touches: changes/add-greeting/tests/
- done when: three test files exist, one per scenario, and each
  fails at the base commit set for its stated reason

### T6 Test suggestions
- role: test
- repo: space
- after: [T1, T2]
- runs: mesh
- needs: any
- serves: [R1, R2]
- done when: every suggestion routed to the test agent is tested or
  declined with a reason

### T7 Verify
- role: test
- repo: space
- after: [T1, T2, T3, T6]
- runs: mesh
- needs: any
- serves: [R1, R2]
- steps: run every project-level test in changes/add-greeting/tests/
  and tests/, each affected repo's unit tests, and every quality
  check the spec declares, at the commit set of the brief
- done when: an evidence record is filed with a result for every
  scenario, unit suite and declared quality check

## 7 Review tasks

### T4 Review of T1
- role: review
- repo: alpha
- after: [T1]
- runs: local
- needs: any
- serves: [R1]
- done when: changes/add-greeting/tasks/T1-review.md holds a verdict

### T5 Review of T2
- role: review
- repo: beta
- after: [T2]
- runs: local
- needs: any
- serves: [R2]
- done when: changes/add-greeting/tasks/T2-review.md holds a verdict

### T8 Whole-change review
- role: review
- repo: space
- after: [T7]
- runs: local
- needs: any
- serves: [R1, R2]
- done when: changes/add-greeting/tasks/T8-review.md holds a verdict

## 8 Integrate task

### T9 Integrate
- role: lead
- repo: space
- after: [T7, T8]
- runs: local
- needs: any
- serves: [R1, R2]
- docs: the README of alpha and of beta; no open plan depends on this
  change
- done when: merged in depends order, tests promoted, pins advanced,
  final report filed

## 9 Test map

| Scenario | Test | Mode | Writes it |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1.S1 | test_R1_S1_default_greeting | inspect | T3 |
| R1.S2 | test_R1_S2_name_too_long | inspect | T3 |
| R2.S1 | test_R2_S1_startup_line | inspect | T3 |

## 10 Dependency summary

T1 and T3 start at the go. T2 waits for T1. The longest chain is T1, T2, T6,
T7, T8, T9. No two tasks touch a common file.

## Self-review

Every requirement maps to a build task (R1 to T1, R2 to T2). Every scenario
maps to a test. No step says TBD. Names and types agree across tasks. Every
task has role, after, runs and done-when.

## Questions for the spec

None.

## Spec
changes/add-greeting/spec.md

## Interface contract
- `alpha`: `greeting(name: str | None = None) -> str`, in `alpha/greeting.py`.
  With no name it returns `hello, demo`. A name of more than 64 code points
  raises `ValueError`, whose message names the 64-character limit.
- `beta`: `python3 -m beta`, run in the `beta` checkout with the `alpha`
  checkout beside it, prints `greeting()` as its first line.

## Global constraints
- "The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points." (spec,
  Open calls 1)
- "its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of start
  (wall time)" (spec, R2.S1)
- Every number carries its unit.

## Test map
| Scenario | Test | Mode | Writes it |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1.S1 | test_R1_S1_default_greeting | inspect | T3 |
| R1.S2 | test_R1_S2_name_too_long | inspect | T3 |
| R2.S1 | test_R2_S1_startup_line | inspect | T3 |

## Start from
- base commit set: {space: the space commit that files this brief, alpha: a1a1a1a, beta: b2b2b2b, gamma: c3c3c3c}
- commit set under test: {space: the space commit that files this brief, alpha: d4d4d4d, beta: e5e5e5e, gamma: c3c3c3c}

- quality: the spec has no Quality section, so `quality: none-declared`.
- regression suite: every regression test in `tests/` at the space commit
  above, each under its key.

## Result goes to
- evidence: changes/add-greeting/evidence/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>.md, with
  `commit_set` naming space, alpha, beta and gamma
- report: changes/add-greeting/evidence/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-T7-report.md
